given: A published release with four assets.
when: Installation downloads and verifies the assets.
then: The compiler and the build record are both authenticated while the result folder does not exist yet, and the installed bytes match the downloaded bytes.

title: The version command reports the current build identity
given: A built stego binary.
when: stego version runs with --json.
then: The build identity in the output equals the compiler's current build identity.

title: Apply writes the current build identity into the record
given: A project ready for apply, and a legacy record with no compiler build.
when: Apply runs, then plan and apply run again on the legacy record.
then: The record holds the current build identity, the legacy record gains it, and a repeated plan changes nothing.
notes: This test calls the compiler in process, which is level unit. A use case test counts only at the level an actor uses, so it does not prove the requirement until a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: Every file apply leaves in the output folder is in the record
given: A new project with a declaration for the rest-crud archetype.
when: The service author runs stego apply.
then: Each file in out/ has an entry in .stego/state.yaml.
notes: ST-GEN-INV01 covers the interrupted apply, where output and record must also change as one.

title: A YAML parser alone reads every file and hash from the record
given: A project after stego apply.
when: The test reads .stego/state.yaml with a YAML parser and no STEGO code.
then: Each listed file exists in out/, and its listed hash is the SHA-256 of its content.

title: The record carries format version 1 and exactly the fields documented for it
given: A project after stego apply.
when: The test reads the record's fields.
then: format_version is 1, every field is in the list for version 1, and every field apply always writes is present.
notes: specs/state-format.md describes the format. A change to a field breaks the test, so the change must update the list, and with it the format version.

title: The drift check fails when a generated file no longer matches its hash
given: A project with applied output and recorded file hashes.
when: A generated file is edited by hand and drift detection runs.
then: The result reports drift.
notes: This test calls the compiler in process, which is level unit. A use case test counts only at the level an actor uses, so it does not prove the requirement until a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: The drift command fails and names a generated file that no longer matches its hash
given: A project after stego apply, where stego drift passes.
when: A generated file is edited by hand and stego drift runs.
then: stego drift fails and prints the path of the edited file.

title: A changed component generator shows as an update in the next plan
given: A project applied from one generator output.
when: The generator produces new content and plan runs again.
then: The plan marks the generated file as an update.
notes: This test calls the compiler in process, which is level unit. A use case test counts only at the level an actor uses, so it does not prove the requirement until a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: A new generation run restores generated output with no hand edit
given: A project with applied output.
when: A generated file is edited by hand, then plan and apply run.
then: The plan names the file as an update, and apply restores the generated content with no drift left.
notes: This test calls the compiler in process, which is level unit. A use case test counts only at the level an actor uses, so it does not prove the requirement until a test runs the stego command end to end. Apply replaces the hand edit here with no permission. When ST-GEN-UC03-R03 is built, this test must state that the run may replace hand edits.

title: A registry change that does not affect output changes no generated file
given: A project with applied output and a recorded registry digest.
when: A comment is added to a component declaration, and plan and apply run.
then: The record gains the new registry digest, every generated file stays unchanged, and a repeated plan changes nothing.
notes: This test calls the compiler in process, which is level unit. A use case test counts only at the level an actor uses, so it does not prove the requirement until a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: Two projects from one declaration get identical files, and a repeated apply changes nothing
given: Two new projects with the same declaration, registry and compiler.
when: stego apply runs three times in each project.
then: The two projects hold byte-identical files, record included, and the third apply prints No changes and changes nothing.
notes: Not proof yet. The first apply writes go.mod but records it as missing, so the second apply rewrites the record. The test allows that one change to the record until it is fixed; then the test must require that the second apply changes nothing, and this record becomes automated.

title: Apply deletes the files of a removed collection
given: A project after stego apply with two collections.
when: One collection is removed from the declaration and stego apply runs.
then: Each file the record no longer lists is gone from out/.
notes: Not proof yet. Apply also deletes such a file when it was edited by hand, which the requirement forbids. That half waits for ST-GEN-UC03-R03, the refusal of hand edits.

title: An apply that fails validation names the failure and changes no project file
given: A project after stego apply.
when: The declaration gets a field whose min_length is above its max_length, and stego apply runs.
then: stego apply fails with an error that names min_length, and every project file keeps its content.
notes: ST-GEN-INV09-T covers the generator and assembler failures in the compiler.

title: Plan leaves the output folder and the record unchanged
given: A new project, and then the same project after stego apply with a changed declaration.
when: stego plan runs.
then: On the new project, service.yaml stays the only file. After apply, the plan shows an update and every project file keeps its content.
notes: stego plan saves no plan today, so it saves none outside .stego/. When saved plans exist, this test must also show that the plan file is the only file written, under .stego/.

title: The plan names each file that apply then creates, updates or deletes, and the record change
given: A project after stego apply.
when: The declaration loses a collection and gains a field, stego plan runs, then stego apply runs.
then: Each file apply creates, updates or deletes, and the record, is named in the plan with that action, and the plan names nothing else.
